t.6.1: Aṣṭāvakra said: I am infinite like space, and the world of nature is like a pot. This is true knowledge; therefore there is neither renouncing it, nor grasping it, nor dissolving it.
t.6.2: I am like the great ocean, and that manifold world is like a wave. This is knowledge, and so there is no renouncing of it, no grasping, no dissolution.
t.6.3: I am That, like the mother-of-pearl, and the imagined universe is like the silver seen in it: this is knowledge. So for this there is no renouncing, no grasping, and no dissolving.
t.6.4: "I am in all beings, and all beings are in me": such is knowledge. So for this there is neither renouncing, nor grasping, nor dissolution.
